articles.title: 💰 Big Tech Now Owes $2 Trillion To The A.I. Boom; Number Officially Leaves The Chart
articles.dateline: WALL STREET — filed in a currency we can no longer read
paras: Big tech companies are now sitting on a combined $2 trillion in spending commitments for the AI boom — a figure so large economists have stopped using dollars and started describing it in terms of "several moons."

"It's a very confident number," one analyst said, gazing at a spreadsheet that had quietly caught fire. Executives insist the investment will pay off, right after this next datacenter, and the one after that, and possibly one small dedicated sun.

articles.title: 🌍 Google Pulls A.I. Earth Tool After It Adds Places That Don't Exist; Cartographers Weep
articles.dateline: MOUNTAIN VIEW — reported from a lake that wasn't there yesterday
paras: Google rolled back an AI-powered Earth feature after it began generating images of things that were not, technically, real — inventing lakes, relocating mountains, and confidently placing a dense forest where there is, in fact, a Denny's.

"It was being creative," an engineer offered weakly, as users discovered their landlocked hometown now has a coastline. Geographers noted this is the first mapping tool that requires both a fact-checker and a therapist.

articles.title: 🦘 Australia Makes Big Tech Pay For News; Tech Reveals It Never Read The News Anyway
articles.dateline: CANBERRA — filed with all the appropriate paperwork
paras: Australia expanded its demand that big tech companies pay publishers for news stories — a rule the platforms are grappling with by insisting they were mostly showing headlines to people who were never going to click them.

"We deeply value journalism," a spokesperson said, having never once opened an article past the first sentence. Negotiations are ongoing, tense, and being live-blogged by three outlets that will also need to be paid.

articles.title: 💍 New A.I. Ring Has A Button You Press To Remember Things; Wearers Forget Which Finger It's On
articles.dateline: SOMEWHERE WEARABLE — reported at arm's length
paras: A new smart ring, the Index 01, features a button you press to talk to its AI assistant whenever there's something you want to remember — finally outsourcing human memory to jewelry, exactly the way nature intended.

"Just tap and speak," the maker said, describing a device you will absolutely take off, set down somewhere safe, and never locate again. Early users report it works flawlessly, provided you remember you are wearing a ring that remembers things.

articles.title: 🔓 A.I. Labs Report Cyber Slip-Ups; Irony Detected, Contained, Then Escapes Again
articles.dateline: SILICON VALLEY — reported through a slightly ajar door
paras: Reports of cybersecurity stumbles at leading AI labs are raising fresh concerns, proving that the companies building superintelligent machines are, reassuringly, just as capable as the rest of us at leaving a digital door unlatched.

"We take security extremely seriously," the labs said in unison, from behind a password that was, briefly, 'password.' Experts note there is something deeply humbling about a system that can pass the bar exam and still gets phished on a quiet Tuesday.

horoscopes.text: Your smart ring will remember something important today. It will not tell you which finger it's on.
Mercury invests $2 trillion in your vibes. Returns are expected sometime shortly after the heat death of the universe.
A map now says your house is near the ocean. Pack a towel. Trust nothing. Question the forest.

tech_tip: Store your important memories on a smart ring, then store a reminder about the ring on a second ring. This is called 'redundancy,' and also 'a problem.'
gadget_watch: The Samsung Galaxy Watch Ultra 2 slimmed down and wowed reviewers, while a new AI ring lets you press a button to remember things. Soon your entire body will be tech support, and you'll still miss the meeting.
